search_scope: Bounded targeted ordinary-NAND whole-row tiling / padding / divisibility / hardware-aware tiling audit; not an exhaustive novelty search.

sources.title: AiF: Accelerating On-Device LLM Inference Using In-Flash Processing
sources.read_depth: Re-read Fig.14 on-chip command/computation paragraphs, §5.2 aif_post/aif_gemv and footnotes 8–9, Table 2; previously read broader architecture. Publisher search extract available; direct DOI open returned 403 this round.
sources.evidence: Public description gives input dimension, block ID, block offset and page count; aif_post uses equal-sized submatrices; footnote 9 allows a submatrix crossing blocks to become two operations.
sources.relation: Direct ordinary NAND full-row baseline and native address/cost constraints. The inspected sections do not provide an unequal whole-row work/depth frontier or the gcd packing lemma.
sources.limit: No proof from these fields of output dtype, desired-row cutoff, cross-block partial-row accumulation or arbitrary plane-private inputs.

sources.title: Cambricon-LLM: A Chiplet-Based Hybrid Architecture for On-Device Inference of 70B LLM
sources.read_depth: Re-read §IV-B–C, §V-A–B and Fig.7; prior round also read setup/selected results.
sources.evidence: Page-sized atomic tiles, channel/compute-core partitioning, same-channel input broadcast; minimizes input/output movement under fixed tile area, then balances NPU/flash work.
sources.relation: Strong direct hardware-aware flash tiling prior: page/parallelism-aware matrix mapping and input reuse are already established. Its inspected construction is 2D atomic tiling with NPU collaboration, not the whole-row-only ordinary-wave rounding frontier.
sources.limit: This does not establish priority of every whole-row specialization; public code/complete numerical return ABI not verified.

sources.title: Matrix Multiplication Background User’s Guide
sources.read_depth: Read §§2.3, 3.1 Tile Quantization and 3.2 Wave Quantization plus document date.
sources.evidence: Explains padding/work inflation from nondivisible tile sizes, tile-efficiency versus parallelism, and tail-wave inefficiency when tile counts do not fill multiprocessors.
sources.relation: Established terminology and mechanism-level precedent for integer tiling/parallelism discontinuities. The NAND complete-row divisibility result is an elementary specialization, not a new number-theory contribution.
sources.limit: GPU wave means a scheduling wave across SMs, not a NAND four-plane read. Its timings or native semantics cannot be imported.

sources.title: Felix: Optimizing Tensor Programs with Gradient Descent
sources.read_depth: Read title/abstract/intro plus §3.3 constraint/divisibility handling, beginning of §3.4 and §4 implementation; not a full-paper reread.
sources.evidence: Searches hardware tensor schedules including tiling; explicitly handles divisibility constraints by rounding to legal integer factors and validates/generated schedules.
sources.relation: General compiler prior against claiming integer legality constraints, factor enumeration or schedule search as new. Does not directly study ordinary NAND complete-row GEMV wave rounding.
sources.limit: GPU tensor-program compiler; no NAND command lowering, no opaque GEMV-row ABI certificate established by this paper.

negative_finding: No inspected primary source directly states the same whole-row ordinary-read exact-work versus least-depth frontier with a physical/numeric lowering certificate. This bounded negative is not a proof of originality. FlexLLM and DIAMoND full texts remain unread/unavailable in earlier legal-access attempts.
